messages:
sarah_sales: Quick heads-up — Acme POC is blocked. Dev reporting 401 on every request after switching to the new API key.

alex_se: Oof. Which endpoint and do they see any error body? 401 could be key invalid or org mismatch.

mike_eng: I grabbed the raw logs from their app. They include an X-Org-Id header set to their tenant id. Response body is: 'unauthorized: tenant not found' — weird.

sarah_sales: Right. Account team says they rotated creds per our docs. Key shows active in dashboard. They attempted curl from laptop and got same 401.

jess_sol: Can you paste the curl they used? Also are they using the org/project headers or the tenant-binding param? Our POC keys are org-scoped.

sarah_sales: They used this:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_ABC123" \
  -H "X-Org-Id: org-99999" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello"}'
```

Response: 401 + JSON {"error":"unauthorized: tenant not found"}

mike_eng: That error means the key is bound to a different org. Likely sk_test_ABC123 belongs to org-55555 but they sent X-Org-Id org-99999. Our auth layer validates header vs key binding.

alex_se: Did they create the key in the prod console vs the POC sandbox? Common mistake is creating a key in their prod-linked org.

sarah_sales: Confirmed: key was created by their SRE in their main account; it's bound to org-55555. They assumed X-Org-Id could override binding.

liz_cs: Ok. Two paths: 1) recreate a key scoped to their POC org (preferred), or 2) remove X-Org-Id so the API uses key-bound org. Which do they want?

andrew_sec: From security side, we shouldn't recommend removing X-Org-Id — better to issue correct-scoped key or adjust bindings. Also check token scopes — make sure it has project.read and inference.write for the model.

mike_eng: I repro'd locally by swapping headers. When header and key mismatch we log: "authz: tenant mismatch: key_org=org-55555 header_org=org-99999". I'll attach an excerpt to ticket.

```
[2026-03-18T14:02:11Z] INFO auth: token=sk_test_ABC123 key_org=org-55555 header_org=org-99999 result=deny reason="tenant mismatch"
```

sarah_sales: Customer asks how long to fix — they're demoing tomorrow.

jess_sol: Fastest: we create a short-lived key bound to their demo org and share secure link. I can do that if sales approves.

alex_se: Go ahead Jess, but mark it as test/demo key and add expiration. Also log the request in case of abuse.

liz_cs: I'll draft the email to them: explain binding, steps to create correct key, and offer us to generate a demo key. Also include pricing note: demo tokens are free but usage > 100k tokens will need conversion to billed account.

andrew_sec: Also add in the security Q answer: keys are org-scoped, bindings enforced server-side; we rotate keys on request and provide audit logs. Add link to our KMS doc.

mike_eng: For completeness, I pushed a tiny guard to dev to return the error with more actionable text: "Key bound to org {key_org}; remove X-Org-Id or create key in target org." Will roll in next 30m. deploy-bot: rolling.

deploy-bot: deployment queued — slot in 2m.

sarah_sales: Thanks team. Jess — can you generate that demo key and post it here as a secure share (or DM)? Also ping me when done, I'll coordinate with Acme.

jess_sol: On it. Creating key with expiry 24h and limited to inference scope. Will DM the link.

liz_cs: Email ready; will include repro steps, the curl snippet, and next steps. Will CC security.

sarah_sales: Perfect. Follow-up: please add a short note to the POC ticket about the root cause so we don't repeat.

mike_eng: Added ticket note with logs and mitigation steps. Ticket #POC-4822.

sarah_sales: Closing the swarm — will reopen if any more 401s. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
